# Orihon

Orihon is a TypeScript browser mapping library.

For AI-generated maps prefer `orihon/ai`. It accepts versioned, JSON-only scenes and
machine-readable commands. For agent-native sessions (intents + browser tools) see
`docs/AI_SESSIONS.md` and `docs/AI_AGENT_SESSION_PROMPT.md`. For ordinary application code
prefer `orihon/easy`.

Imports:

    import { createMap } from "orihon/easy";
    import {
      createAISession,
      createAIAgentSession,
      listAISessionTools,
      installAIWebMCPTools,
      createAIAGUIAdapter,
      createMemoryAISessionStore,
      restoreAIAgentSession,
      applyScene
    } from "orihon/ai";
    import "orihon/orihon.css";

Coordinate rules:
- Orihon AI coordinates are objects: `{ "lat": 55.75, "lng": 37.61 }`.
- Coordinate arrays are not accepted by the AI API.
- GeoJSON remains standard longitude-first: `[37.61, 55.75]`.

Scene rules (createAISession / orihon_execute):
- Use `version: 1`.
- Every layer has a stable, unique `id`.
- Layer types are `marker`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `geojson`, and `raster`.
- Popup and tooltip content is plain text: `{ "text": "Moscow" }`.
- Functions, DOM nodes, class instances, `undefined`, and non-finite numbers are rejected.

Agent-session rules (createAIAgentSession / session.call):
- Prefer `orihon.plan` semantic intents over inventing layer/command JSON.
- Goals: `show_places`, `create_visit_route`, `update_points` (plus stress-test goals when enabled).
- Browser tools: `map.get_viewport`, `map.set_viewport`, `map.get_selection`, `map.set_selection`,
  `map.open_popup`, `map.close_popup`.
- `local.viewport` includes `center`, `zoom`, and `bounds` `{south,west,north,east}` — use bounds
  at high zoom; center alone is not the visible rectangle.
- One session id ↔ one map instance. Point `category`: `alpha` | `beta` | `gamma` | `alert`.
- Same tool list everywhere: `listAISessionTools`, WebMCP (`installAIWebMCPTools`), AG-UI
  (`createAIAGUIAdapter`). Do not invent a second vocabulary.
- Optional persistence: `createAISessionRecord` / `restoreAIAgentSession` / `createMemoryAISessionStore`.
- Auth, multi-node sync, and DB are host concerns.

Server/agent rules:
- `createAICommandEngine()` is headless and owns canonical revisioned JSON state.
- Prefer `createAIIntentTool(createAIAgentRuntime(engine))` for semantic goals; it plans through
  registered ObjectManager and Route Model capabilities and commits atomically.
- Use `show_places` for markers without a route; `create_visit_route` when a tour/path is needed.
- `create_visit_route` routes are reactive by default: collection changes trigger engine-side
  replanning without another model call.
- `createAIHTTPHandler(engine)` exposes snapshot, command, and SSE endpoints.
- Semantic HTTP endpoints expose capabilities, compact context, intent preview, intent commit, and place search.
- `createAIAgentSession({ id, engine, map?, projection? })` is the agent-facing session; `session.call` routes browser tools and semantic intents.
- `session.observeBrowser({ selection, viewport, editable })` and `subscribeUser` mirror map
  clicks/drags/pans into session local state (and optionally the engine).
- `createAIHTTPHandler(engine, { sessions })` exposes session create + scoped context/intents/SSE/local.
- `createAIMapProjection(map)` applies server events in the browser.
- Live domain entities use `objects.*` commands and stable GeoJSON feature IDs.
- Object deltas flow through `FeatureSource` into `ObjectManager`.
- Named point maps can use `points.replace` with declarative popups, circular `visual.image`, hover-first `visual.label`, and `viewport.mode:"fit"`.
- `presentation.defaults.visual` applies to points that omit `visual`, with either a shared
  `image.url`, a shared `label`, or both.
- `{ "op": "clear" }` resets the whole AI map — scene layers, collections and routes.
  Use `{ "op": "clear", "ids": [...] }` for single layers and `objects.clear` for one collection.
- A `viewport.mode:"fit"` hint expires with the revision that produced it; later commands never
  revive it, so the camera is fitted once and the user keeps control afterwards.
- `restoreAIAgentSession` / `engine.replaceSnapshot` rebuild state without events — call
  `projection.applySnapshot(engine.getSnapshot())` to repaint an attached map.
- `route.plan` orders an existing point collection and projects its RouteResult through RoutingLayer.
- `createAIEngineTool(engine, { profile })` supports `full`, `scene`, `objects`, `points`, `routes`, and `readonly` schemas.
- Engine tool results are compact by default; HTTP and SSE retain complete revisioned events.
